messages.subject: Using plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace for unidimensional data?
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I wondered whether it is possible at all to plot a 3D phylomorphospace using the pertinent geomorph function in data which has only one dimension (i.e. coordinates in a single axis)? 

I tried (adding a column of zeros or ones) and in both cases I get this error (for the pca):

Error in seq.default(ym - 1/5 * rX, yM + 1/5 * rX, by = (xM - xm) * 7/(5 *  : 
  invalid '(to - from)/by'


Best, 

Guille

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Using plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace for unidimensional data?
parts:
Guille,

 

If there is only a single variable, one does not have a phylomorphospace: one has a number line. 

 

The closest visualization to a phylomorphospace along a single axis that I am aware of is a traitgram (sensu Evans et al. 2009).  Here, the phenotypic values are plotted on the Y-axis and time on the X-axis.  The function ‘phenogram’ in phytools can do this.


Best,


Dean

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Using plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace for unidimensional data?
parts:
Guille,

 

Those redundancies would likely cause some issues with the standard phylomorphospace function in geomorph because of the invariant dimensions due to the landmarks being found on a plane. Though I must admit this is a suspicion only: I have not tried it with such data to know for certain.

 

But in general one could still do a PCA because the data presumably have variation in the 12 y-variables. So conceptually a phylomorphospace plot is possible through some other means.  

 

One solution here is to perform the PCA in R (e.g., using prcomp), and then use the phylomorphospace function in phytools for the plot. Note that this particular function does not do the PCA automatically; the user must provide it with 2 axes that define the phylomorphospace. The most reasonable choice would be to use PC1 and PC2.

Dean
